title: The impact of home use of dental plaque disclosing agent (chewing tablets) on oral hygiene in high caries risk schoolchildren: A single-blinded randomized controlled clinical trial with 3 months follow-up
summary: This study will explore whether using a special tablet at home that reveals hidden dental plaque can enhance the oral hygiene of schoolchildren at high risk for tooth decay. We will compare two groups: one receiving standard brushing advice and another using the plaque-disclosing tablet weekly. By assessing the dental condition of their teeth and gums over three months, we aim to determine if this tool provides a significant improvement in maintaining children's oral health.

interventions.name: Usual motivation and instructions for oral hygiene as part of regular individual prophylaxis (including recommendation of weekly use of fluoride gel) as well as counselling for tooth brushing by the caregiver if necessary.
like group in Arm 1; additionally weekly use of dental plaque disclosing agent (Plaquefinder, tablets, Curaprox, Switzerland) before the weekly use of fluoride gel

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Children aged 6 - 12 years 
- Caries risk child:  "dmft/DMFT > 0“ or „dmft/DMFT = 0 with at least one active initial carious lesion" or "MIH". 
- Child scheduled for in-office oral examination and individual caries prevention session including disclosure of plaque  
- Insufficient oral hygiene (visible plaque without disclosing agent) 
- Willingness to use on a weekly basis highly concentrated fluoride gel & plaque disclosing tablets. 
- Willing to come for prophylaxis appointment approx. 3 months later. 
- Signed written informed consent form for study participation.
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with pain or acute oral symptoms to be treated 
- Patients with systemic diseases that require special attention during their dental treatment 
- Patients with fixed orthodontic appliances 
- Patients who are already using a plaque disclosing agents at home on a regular basis 
- Caregiver/ children who refuse to participate in the study 
- Allergy against ingredients of disclosing agent
